title: Activation governor playbook and telemetry matrix (wip)
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook for the activation governor: the lightweight orchestration and safety layers we use to turn on changes (model variants, routing rules, optimization knobs) with measurable guardrails. Goal: reduce blast radius, make rollouts predictable, and standardize observability for cross-functional teams.

Scope
- Applies to: model updates (hosted/dedicated/private), routing/policy changes, major config toggles (batching, quant profiles), and new product surface experiments.
- Not in scope: infra-only node upgrades (SRE runbooks exist), customer billing changes.

Quick overview (one-liner)
Activation Governor = canary + telemetry matrix + human/automated gates + communication choreography. Think of it as the "experiment switch" with eyes and brakes.

Core principles (short)
- Small early exposure: start with <0.5% traffic for risky model behavior changes.
- Signal parity: ensure canary traffic mirrors production in client headers, prompt surface distribution, and request size.
- Observability-first: no activation without dashboards and alarms in place.
- Fast reversion path: one-click rollback and automated fallback model/policy.
- Cross-functional ownership: product owns hypothesis, eng owns ops play, SRE owns infra safety.

Actors & responsibilities
- Release owner (product/PM): owns hypothesis, success criteria, comms cadence.
- Release lead (eng): coordinates rollout steps, config changes, rollback trigger thresholds.
- Telemetry steward (observability): implements dashboards, event markers, logs sampling.
- Oncall SRE: ensures infra limits, throttles capacity, authorizes emergency rollbacks.
- Customer Success: preps comms for impacted customers if exposure >10%.

Telemetry matrix (minimum signals to monitor before and during activation)
- Availability & Errors:
  - 5xx rate (global + per-route) — rolling 5m, 95th percentile
  - Client-side timeout rate (SDK)
  - Retries triggered by router
- Latency:
  - P50/P90/P99 tail latency for token generation, per-model and per-route
  - Cold-start latency if model variant requires new instances
- Cost/Throughput:
  - Tokens/sec, average tokens per request
  - GPU utilization and queue length on serving nodes
- Quality signals (model-output specific):
  - Safety score (automated classifier) — % flagged
  - Semantic similarity drift vs baseline (embedding cosine distribution)
  - Top-k entropy / temperature sensitivity indicators
  - Customer-facing metric (CTR or downstream conversion) — if applicable
- Data integrity:
  - Request/response size anomalies, truncation, or malformed outputs
  - KV-cache hit rate (if applicable)
- Business & usage:
  - Request volume by client tier, geo, route slice
  - Billing anomalies (sudden cost spike)

Minimum gating thresholds (starter recommendations — tune per-product)
- Safety: if safety flags > 0.5% of canary responses AND absolute delta vs baseline > 0.3pp -> pause and investigate.
- Errors: if 5xx increases by >50% relative to baseline AND exceeds 0.2% absolute -> rollback to previous model.
- Latency: P99 latency increase >30% AND P90 increase >20% -> scale/rollback decision.
- Cost: per-token cost increase >25% with no quality gain -> rollback.
- Business metric: any statistically significant negative shift (defined in hypothesis) over 24h -> hold.

Activation patterns (playground of options)
1) Timeboxed microcanary (default for model behavior): 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1% over 6–24 hours with manual hold at each step.
2) Weighted ramp with automated checks: 1%, 5%, 20% with automated gates enforced by the governor (requires robust telemetry hooks).
3) Cohort-based exposure: allocate to specific geo + customer tier + internal-staff cohort (useful for client-specific features).
4) Shadow canary (only logs outputs): run canary model in shadow, compare outputs using automated scoring, no direct traffic exposure. Good for quality-only experiments.
5) Synthetic traffic first: if real traffic is sparse for the slice, replay recorded prompts to stress test and measure resource impact before live exposure.

A/B testing guidance (when experiment is an A/B)
- Hypothesis templating (short): "If we switch to Model X for reranking, user click-through on recommendations increases by >= 3% with no increase in safety flags."
- Sample sizing: coordinate with analytics — avoid underpowered experiments. If rollout must be fast, prefer sequential canary then short A/B after stable.
- Slicing: keep experiment slicing orthogonal to other rollouts. Use feature flags and route metadata to avoid contamination.
- Aggregation windows: define short-term (1–3h) signal sweep for safety/ops; long-term (24–72h) for product metrics.

Operational checklist (pre-activation)
- [ ] Dashboard runbook exists and is shared (link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Health alarms configured for the telemetry matrix with paging thresholds.
- [ ] Rollback artifact/version pinned and smoke test validated.
- [ ] Canary slice selection documented (percent, cohorts), and cohort parity validated via distribution checks.
- [ ] Communication stub: Slack channel + escalation list created.
- [ ] QA: safety checks and a small set of golden prompts validated manually.
- [ ] Capacity: infra can sustain 3x expected canary amplification (safety headroom).

During-activation playbook (operational rhythm)
- Step 0: mark activation start in timeline (telemetry steward).
- Step 1: open canary at initial percent, annotate dashboards with version tag.
- Step 2: 30–60 minute observation window for basic signals (errors, latency, safety).
- Step 3: if all gates green -> proceed to next percent or schedule automated ramp step.
- Step 4: if any gate trips -> immediate hold and triage. Release lead to run triage script (below).
- Step 5: after reaching target exposure, continue long-form observation window (24–72h) for product signals.

Triage script (fast checklist when gate trips)
- Snapshot current logs and mark timeline.
- Rollback to previous variant if error/safety gates violated.
- If not obvious, scale canary down to 0.1% and keep collecting logs for 2h.
- Escalate to SRE if infra (GPU queueing, OOM, excessive retries) shows up.
- Summarize immediate findings in Slack incident channel and start longer RCA if needed.

Communication templates (short)
- Slack (activation start): "[activation] Starting canary vX for route Y at 2025-01-08 18:00 UTC. Initial slice 0.5%. Dashboards: <dash link>. Oncall: @sre-oncall. Release lead: @avery. Post any anomalies in #rollouts-watch."
- Slack (rollback): "[rollback] Rolling back vX -> vW for route Y due to error spike at 18:42 UTC. Action: switch traffic, scaling, and alerting in effect. Postmortem: JIRA-4862."

Open questions / notes
- How strict should automated rollbacks be for safety flags vs infra errors? (product wants safety conservative; infra prefers manual for noisy signals).
- Need a standardized sampling policy for request/response capture (privacy).
- Build a small "canary simulator" that can re-run historical traffic slices through model variants for pre-activation validation. (tracked in GH PR).

Immediate TODOs (short list)
- [ ] Telemetry steward to add safety-tagged example extraction in dashboards (Diego).
- [ ] Draft a short-runbook card in PagerDuty for "canary-safety-trip" with clear next actions (Linh).
- [ ] Prototype synthetic traffic runner and link to this doc (Omar).

Appendix: quick checklist for small teams launching frequent microreleases
- Keep early exposure tiny (0.05–0.2%).
- Use internal staff + sandbox customers as first cohort.
- Always have dark-shadow comparison before large exposure.
- When in doubt, prioritize rollback — faster to iterate than to recover from bad public behavior.

-- end working draft --

Notes: this is an intentionally lean operational doc aimed at teams shipping model and inference changes. It should be used alongside the more procedural "staged-deployment-signal-runbook" (see linked artifacts) and product-level experiment contracts. Please comment inline — this is a living doc.
